items.title: Section: The Five Marks a Teacher Guides a Beginner to Grasp

items.zh: 謂善通達修瑜伽師，最初於彼依瑜伽行初修業者，如是教誨：善來賢首！汝等今者應依三種取相因緣，或見、或聞、或心比度增上分別，取五種相。一、厭離相，二、欣樂相，三、過患相，四、光明相，五、了別事相。
items.en: A teacher well versed in yogic practice, at the very outset, instructs a beginner newly taking up yogic conduct thus: "Welcome, excellent one! You should now, by way of three conditions for grasping a mark — seeing, hearing, or empowered discernment through inward reflection — grasp five marks. First, the mark of revulsion. Second, the mark of delight. Third, the mark of danger. Fourth, the mark of brightness. Fifth, the mark of discerning the object."

items.zh: 問：若依瑜伽行初修業者是其貪行，由不淨觀方可調伏，云何教彼取五種相？答：應如是教誨：

items.title: The Mark of Revulsion: Grasped Through Hearing and Through Seeing

items.zh: 善來賢首！汝等隨所依止彼彼聚落村邑而住於中，若聞所餘彼彼村邑聚落，或男或女，先受安樂，後遭苦厄。或彼男女自遭重病，命終殞沒。或彼男女所有知識、親戚、眷屬遭如是苦。或彼聚落村邑邊際喪失財寶，或是他來強敵所作，或火所燒，或水所漂，或由惡作而有喪失，或由不善修營事業而有喪失，或由不善處分事業而有喪失，或為非愛共財得便而有喪失，或由家火而有喪失。
items.en: "Welcome, excellent one! Wherever village or town you dwell in, if you hear that in some other village or town a man or woman, having first enjoyed ease, later met with suffering and hardship; or that such a man or woman was himself struck by grave illness and died; or that such a man or woman's friends, relatives, or family met with such suffering; or that in the vicinity of some village or town, wealth was lost — whether seized by an invading enemy, consumed by fire, swept away by flood, lost through evil deeds done in the past, or lost through poorly managed affairs …"

items.zh: 若汝現見，非是傳聞；或即於此村邑聚落，非是所餘村邑聚落；或非是此村邑聚落，亦非他人，即汝自身；先所觸證猛利樂受，後還退失，廣說如前。
items.en: "Or if you yourself directly witness this, not merely hear it secondhand; or if it occurs in this very village where you dwell, not some other; or if it is not even another person but you yourself — having first experienced intense pleasure, only to have it later decline — extensively explained as before."

items.title: Section: Deep Revulsion Towards Both Decline and Flourishing Alike

items.zh: 汝既如是聞已、見已，應當生起深心厭患。如是生死甚為重苦，所得自體極大艱辛，而於其中有如是等自他衰損差別可得。謂病衰損、壽命衰損、眷屬衰損、財寶衰損，病、病法性，死、死法性。復有一類，淨戒衰損、正見衰損。由是因緣，彼諸眾生於現法中住諸苦惱，於當來世往諸惡趣。諸興盛者，雖現法中住諸安樂，於當來世往諸善趣，而是無常，於彼無常現可證得。若有領受興盛事者，後時衰損定當現前；諸有領受衰損事者，後時興盛難可現前。諸興盛事，皆是難得易失壞法。
items.en: Having thus heard and seen these things, you should give rise to deep revulsion: this cycle of birth and death is a truly grave suffering, and the very existence one obtains within it is fraught with great hardship — such differentiated declines, both one's own and others', can indeed be found within it … As for flourishing, though in this present life one dwells in ease, and in the life to come proceeds to a fortunate destiny, it is nevertheless impermanent, and this impermanence can be directly verified. Whoever now experiences flourishing will, at some later time, certainly meet with decline; whoever now experiences decline finds flourishing difficult to attain again. Every state of flourishing is a thing hard to gain and easy to lose.

items.zh: 如是汝應深心厭患，極善作意，如理受持。如是處所，難可保信。
我今於是生死流轉，未般涅槃，未解脫心，難可保信如是衰損、興盛二法，勿現我前。勿彼因緣，令我墮在如是處所，生起猛利、剛強、辛楚、不適意苦。即由此事增上力故，我當至誠喜樂於斷，修不放逸。又我如是多安住故，當於無義能作邊際。
items.en: "I am now still transmigrating in birth and death, not yet passed into nirvāṇa, my mind not yet liberated — I cannot be assured that these two states, decline and flourishing, will not appear before me … Through the empowering force of this very reflection, I shall wholeheartedly delight in cutting this off, and cultivate non-heedlessness. And by abiding thus, again and again, I shall be able to bring this meaningless cycle to its very limit."

items.zh: 如是汝應善極作意，如理受持。

items.title: The Mark of Delight Opens: Examining One's Own Precepts

items.zh: 汝取如是厭離相已，復應精勤取欣樂相。當自觀察所受尸羅，為善清淨？為不清淨？我或失念、或不恭敬、或多煩惱、或由無知，於諸學處有所違犯。
items.en: "Having thus grasped the mark of revulsion, you should further diligently grasp the mark of delight. You should examine for yourself whether the precepts you have undertaken are well purified, or not purified — whether, through a lapse of mindfulness, through irreverence, through abundant affliction, or through ignorance, you have transgressed any of the precepts undertaken."

items.zh: 既違犯已，我當如法以其本性增上意樂，於諸學處發起深心，更不毀犯。我於所作當正應作，於非所作不復當作。以要言之，於諸學處，當令增上意樂圓滿，亦令所有加行圓滿。

blocks.text: Fascicle 32 is the treatise's most practical teaching: the actual words a teacher says to a beginner, step by step, from the first marks to the arising of pliancy. It ends with the threshold of the form realm's preparatory concentration.
"Welcome, excellent one!" The teacher asks the beginner to grasp five marks: revulsion, delight, danger, brightness, and the mark of discerning the object, by seeing, hearing, or inner reflection.

"If you hear that in some other town a man or woman, having first enjoyed ease, later met with suffering; or was struck by grave illness and died"; "or if you yourself witness this; or it is not another person but you yourself". Master Cháng Bǎi: three degrees: hearing, seeing, oneself.

"This cycle of birth and death is a grave suffering." Even flourishing is "hard to gain and easy to lose". "I am still transmigrating, my mind not yet liberated; I cannot be assured that decline and flourishing will not appear before me." So one resolves to "bring this meaningless cycle to its limit".

"Examine whether your precepts are well purified, or whether, through a lapse of mindfulness, irreverence, abundant affliction, or ignorance, you have broken any." Master Cháng Bǎi: the mark of delight begins with a clear conscience.
The teacher's voice, "Welcome, excellent one!", is warm. The instruction begins not with technique but with motivation: seeing clearly why one is practising.

quiz.q: Which five marks does the teacher have the beginner grasp, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi say the three conditions are used?
options: revulsion, delight, danger, brightness, discerning the object; seeing and hearing off the cushion, inner reflection while sitting
quiz.why: "First, the mark of revulsion. Second, the mark of delight. Third, the mark of danger. Fourth, the mark of brightness. Fifth, the mark of discerning the object." Master Cháng Bǎi: off the cushion one grasps these five through seeing and hearing; while sitting, through inner reflection — the empowered discernment of thinking and observing.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "inward reflection," one of the three conditions?
options: without seeing or hearing — simply reflecting and inferring in the mind
quiz.why: "You should now, by way of three conditions for grasping a mark — seeing, hearing, or empowered discernment through inward reflection — grasp five marks." Venerable Miào Jìng: "inward reflection" means observing within — I have neither seen nor heard, but my mind infers it this way.

quiz.q: Hearing that "such a person was struck by grave illness and died," what old saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: better a bad life than a good death
seeing others die, my heart burns — not for them, but because my turn is coming
quiz.why: "Or that such a man or woman was himself struck by grave illness and died." Master Cháng Bǎi cites an old saying: "I see others die and my heart burns like fire — not for them, but because my own turn is coming."

quiz.q: "If you directly witness this, not merely hear it." How many conditions for grasping revulsion does Master Cháng Bǎi name?
quiz.why: "Or if you yourself directly witness this, not merely hear it secondhand." Master Cháng Bǎi: there are three conditions for grasping the mark of revulsion — seeing with the eyes, hearing, and inner inference.

quiz.q: "All flourishing is hard to gain and easy to lose." Why does Venerable Miào Jìng say flourishing too should be loathed?
options: decline brings distress, and so does flourishing — the suffering of change
quiz.why: "Every state of flourishing is a thing hard to gain and easy to lose." Venerable Miào Jìng: decline distresses us; flourishing distresses us too — that is the suffering of change.

quiz.q: "Bring 無義 to its limit" — the English says "this meaningless cycle." How do the masters read 無義?
options: Miào Jìng: meaningless activities — stop doing them; Cháng Bǎi: birth-and-death suffering, without benefit
quiz.why: "By abiding thus, again and again, I shall be able to bring this meaningless cycle to its very limit." Venerable Miào Jìng: one may set a limit to meaningless things — stop here and never do them again. Master Cháng Bǎi: "without benefit" here refers to the suffering of birth and death, which is not to be delighted in — hence "meaningless."

quiz.q: Precepts are broken "through lapse of mindfulness or irreverence." How does Master Cháng Bǎi map these to the Vastusaṃgrahaṇī?
options: lapse of mindfulness is heedlessness there; irreverence is disdain
quiz.why: "Whether, through a lapse of mindfulness, through irreverence, through abundant affliction, or through ignorance, you have transgressed any of the precepts." Master Cháng Bǎi: lapse of mindfulness here is the heedlessness spoken of in the Vastusaṃgrahaṇī; irreverence is disdain.
